label: R9
title: Robust optimization
brief: Robust optimization requires a constraint $a_i^\top x\le b_i$ to hold for every coefficient vector in an uncertainty set $U_i$: infinitely many constraints, or equivalently one ill-structured constraint $\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x\le b_i$. The two-variable example with $U=\{a\in\mathbb R^2_+: a_1+a_2\le3\}$ shows the fix: evaluate the inner max analytically ($3\max\{x_1,x_2\}$) and obtain an equivalent LP. For norm uncertainty sets $U_i=\{\bar a_i+\Delta_i^\top u_i: \|u_i\|\le\rho\}$ the inner max is $\bar a_i^\top x$ plus a norm penalty that swaps norms: budget ($\ell_1$) gives $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_\infty$, ellipsoidal ($\ell_2$) gives $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_2$, box ($\ell_\infty$) gives $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_1$; budget and box linearize to LPs, ellipsoidal is conic. For polyhedral sets $\{\bar a_i+u_i: D_iu_i\le d_i\}$, LP duality replaces the inner max with its dual min, giving an LP with extra variables $p_i\ge0$. When that LP is large, a cutting-plane method keeps only the original variables and adds worst-case constraints as they are violated, with special handling when the master is unbounded.
kp: Robust constraint: $a_i^\top x\le b_i$ for all $a_i\in U_i$ $\iff$ $g_i(x):=\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x\le b_i$; tractable when each $g_i$ has a tractable representation.
Example: $U=\{a\in\mathbb R^2_+: a_1+a_2\le3\}$ gives $g(x)=3\max\{x_1,x_2\}$ for $x\ge0$, so $a^\top x\le6\ \forall a\in U$ becomes $x_1\le2$, $x_2\le2$.
Norm uncertainty set: $U_i=\{\bar a_i+\Delta_i^\top u_i: \|u_i\|\le\rho\}$; $\ell_1$ = budget, $\ell_2$ = ellipsoidal, $\ell_\infty$ = box.
Inner max $=\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|$ with the swapped norm: $\ell_1$ set $\to\|\cdot\|_\infty$, $\ell_2\to\|\cdot\|_2$, $\ell_\infty\to\|\cdot\|_1$.
Budget counterpart: $\bar a_i^\top x\pm\rho(\Delta_ix)_j\le b_i$ for all $j$ — an LP with no new variables.
Box counterpart: auxiliary $t_{ij}$ with $-t_{ij}\le(\Delta_ix)_j\le t_{ij}$ and $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\sum_jt_{ij}\le b_i$ — an LP.
Ellipsoidal counterpart $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_2\le b_i$ is a conic program.
Polyhedral: robust constraint $\iff\exists p_i\ge0$ with $p_i^\top D_i=x^\top$ and $\bar a_i^\top x+p_i^\top d_i\le b_i$ (LP duality, inner problem feasible and finite).
Direct polyhedral LP: $n+\sum_i\ell_i$ variables and $m(n+1)$ scalar constraints; cutting planes keep $n$ variables and add constraints only when needed.
Cutting planes: start from the nominal problem, find each row's worst case $\hat a_i$, add $\hat a_i^\top x\le b_i$ if violated by more than $\varepsilon$, stop when no cut is added.

topics.x: A nominal constraint uses one known coefficient vector; a robust one must hold for every $a$ in an uncertainty set $U$, which is a semi-infinite family. Writing it as $\max_{a\in U}a^\top x\le b$ gives one constraint, but an ill-structured one whose left side is itself an optimization problem. The strategy is to replace that max $g_i(x)$ with an equivalent tractable expression.

$U_i=\{\bar a_i+\Delta_i^\top u_i: \|u_i\|\le\rho\}$ perturbs the nominal row $\bar a_i$ through a fixed scaling matrix $\Delta_i$ and a perturbation $u_i$ of size at most $\rho$. The $\ell_1$ ball gives budget uncertainty, the $\ell_2$ ball ellipsoidal uncertainty and the $\ell_\infty$ ball box uncertainty.

The inner problem is $Z_i^*=\bar a_i^\top x+\max_{\|u_i\|\le\rho}u_i^\top(\Delta_ix)$. Over an $\ell_1$ ball this is $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_\infty$, over an $\ell_2$ ball $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_2$, over an $\ell_\infty$ ball $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_1$. These follow from linear algebra, and the $\ell_1$ and $\ell_\infty$ cases also from LP duality.

A max of absolute values is at most $b$ iff every term is, so the budget counterpart becomes $2k_i$ linear constraints. A sum of absolute values needs auxiliary $t_{ij}\ge|(\Delta_ix)_j|$, giving an LP for box uncertainty. The ellipsoidal counterpart keeps a 2-norm and is conic.

For $U_i=\{\bar a_i+u_i: D_iu_i\le d_i\}$, which need not be a norm ball, the inner max $\max\{u_i^\top x: D_iu_i\le d_i\}$ equals the dual $\min\{p_i^\top d_i: p_i^\top D_i=x^\top, p_i\ge0\}$. A min is at most $b$ iff some feasible $p_i$ achieves it, so the robust problem becomes one LP in $(x,\{p_i\})$, at the cost of many extra variables and constraints.

Start with the nominal problem as master, solve, then for each row compute the worst case $\hat a_i=\arg\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x^*$ and add $\hat a_i^\top x\le b_i$ if it is violated by more than $\varepsilon$. Stop when no cut is added. An unbounded master does not prove the robust problem unbounded: take $x^*$ with $c^\top x^*>M$ and cut it off.

cards.b: Nominal: $a^\top x\le b$ for one known $a$. Robust: $a^\top x\le b$ for all $a\in U$ (infinitely many constraints), equivalently $\max_{a\in U}a^\top x\le b$.
cards.x: The max form is ill-structured: evaluating its left side means solving an optimization problem.

cards.f: Robust counterpart of $a_1x_1+a_2x_2\le6$ for all $a\in\{a\in\mathbb R^2_+: a_1+a_2\le3\}$, with $x\ge0$.
cards.b: $\max_{a\in U}a^\top x=3\max\{x_1,x_2\}$, so the constraint is $x_1\le2$, $x_2\le2$.

cards.f: When does a robust LP have a tractable equivalent?
cards.b: When each $g_i(x)=\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x$ has a tractable representation; then $\max c^\top x$ s.t. $g_i(x)\le b_i$, $x\ge0$ is equivalent.
cards.x: The work is all in finding a closed form or dual for $g_i$.

cards.b: $U_i=\{a_i=\bar a_i+\Delta_i^\top u_i: \|u_i\|\le\rho,\ u_i\in\mathbb R^{k_i}\}$: nominal $\bar a_i$, fixed scaling matrix $\Delta_i\in\mathbb R^{k_i\times n}$, perturbation $u_i$, size $\rho\ge0$.

cards.f: Which norm gives which named uncertainty set?
cards.b: $\ell_1$ ball: budget. $\ell_2$ ball: ellipsoidal. $\ell_\infty$ ball: box.
cards.x: Diamond, disk, square around $\bar a_i$ (before scaling by $\Delta_i$).

cards.f: Inner max for each norm uncertainty set.
cards.b: $Z_i^*=\bar a_i^\top x+\max_{\|u_i\|\le\rho}u_i^\top(\Delta_ix)$ $=\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_\infty$ ($\ell_1$ set), $+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_2$ ($\ell_2$ set), $+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_1$ ($\ell_\infty$ set).

cards.x: The adversary spends its whole budget on the single most damaging coordinate.
Every coordinate moves to its worst extreme at once.

cards.b: $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho(\Delta_ix)_j\le b_i$ and $\bar a_i^\top x-\rho(\Delta_ix)_j\le b_i$ for $j=1,\dots,k_i$: $2k_i$ linear constraints.
cards.x: A max is $\le b$ iff every term is $\le b$, so no new variables are needed.

cards.b: Add $t_{ij}\ge0$ with $-t_{ij}\le(\Delta_ix)_j\le t_{ij}$ and $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}t_{ij}\le b_i$.
cards.x: Unlike the max case, a sum of absolute values needs auxiliary variables.

cards.b: Box: linear. Budget: linear. Polyhedral: linear. Ellipsoidal: conic.
cards.x: Only the 2-norm penalty leaves LP territory.

cards.b: $U_i=\{\bar a_i+u_i: D_iu_i\le d_i,\ u_i\in\mathbb R^n\}$ with $D_i\in\mathbb R^{\ell_i\times n}$, $d_i\in\mathbb R^{\ell_i}$. It need not be a norm uncertainty set.
cards.x: Example: $\bar a=(2,2)$ with $-u_1\le1$, $-u_2\le1$, $u_1+u_2\le1$ is a triangle, not a norm ball.

cards.b: Primal: $\max_{u_i}u_i^\top x$ s.t. $D_iu_i\le d_i$. Dual: $\min_{p_i\ge0}p_i^\top d_i$ s.t. $p_i^\top D_i=x^\top$. Robust constraint $\iff\exists p_i\ge0$: $p_i^\top D_i=x^\top$, $\bar a_i^\top x+p_i^\top d_i\le b_i$.
cards.x: 'max $\le b$' is hard; 'min $\le b$' just needs one feasible witness $p_i$.

cards.f: Size of the direct polyhedral LP.
cards.b: $n+\sum_i\ell_i$ variables; $m(n+1)$ scalar constraints excluding nonnegativity ($n$ equalities from $p_i^\top D_i=x^\top$ plus one robust inequality per row). For $m=1000$, $n=100$, $\ell_i=200$: 200,100 variables, 101,000 constraints.
cards.x: Cutting planes keep just the $n=100$ original variables in the master.

cards.b: 1) Master = nominal problem ($\hat U_i=\{\bar a_i\}$). 2) Solve: infeasible $\Rightarrow$ robust infeasible; unbounded $\Rightarrow$ pick $x^*$ with $c^\top x^*>M$; else optimal $x^*$. 3) For each row, $\hat a_i=\arg\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x^*$; if $\hat a_i^\top x^*>b_i+\varepsilon$, add $\hat a_i^\top x\le b_i$. 4) No cut $\Rightarrow$ $x^*$ robust optimal; else back to 2.
cards.x: Master infeasibility is conclusive because the master is a relaxation.

cards.f: Why not stop when the master is unbounded?
cards.b: The master has only some of the robust constraints, so it can be unbounded while the robust problem is finite. Pick $x^*$ with $c^\top x^*>M$ and add any violated worst-case cut to block the direction.
cards.x: Example: $\max_{x\ge0}x$ s.t. $a_1x\le1$, $a_1\in[0,1]$: nominal $a_1=0$ is unbounded; $x^*=101$ yields the cut $x\le1$, then $x^*=1$ is robust optimal.

quiz.q: For a continuous uncertainty set $U$, the robust constraint $a^\top x\le b\ \ \forall a\in U$ represents:
o: Infinitely many linear constraints, one per $a\in U$
A single linear constraint at the nominal $\bar a$
A constraint required to hold with high probability
quiz.e: The constraint must hold for every point of $U$, a semi-infinite family. Enforcing only the nominal $\bar a$ is the non-robust problem.

quiz.q: Nominal: $\max x_1+x_2$ s.t. $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x\ge0$. With $U=\{a\in\mathbb R^2_+: a_1+a_2\le3\}$ and constraint $a^\top x\le6\ \forall a\in U$, what is the robust optimal value?
quiz.e: Worst case $3\max\{x_1,x_2\}\le6$ gives $x_1\le2$, $x_2\le2$, so the optimum is $(2,2)$ with value 4. 6 is the nominal value, ignoring uncertainty.

quiz.q: For $x\ge0$, why is $\max\{a_1x_1+a_2x_2: a\in\mathbb R^2_+, a_1+a_2\le3\}=3\max\{x_1,x_2\}$?
o: A linear function over the triangle peaks at a vertex: $(3,0)$, $(0,3)$ or $(0,0)$
The max is attained at the centroid $(1,1)$
quiz.e: The vertices give $3x_1$, $3x_2$ and 0, so the max is $3\max\{x_1,x_2\}$. An even split gives $1.5(x_1+x_2)\le3\max\{x_1,x_2\}$, never more.

quiz.q: The uncertainty set $\{\bar a+\Delta^\top u: \|u\|_\infty\le\rho\}$ is called:
quiz.e: The $\ell_\infty$ ball is a box. Budget uncertainty is the $\ell_1$ ball.
$|3|+|-4|=7$; $\sqrt{9+16}=5$; $\max\{3,4\}=4$. The $-1$ forgets absolute values; 25 forgets the square root.

quiz.q: With budget uncertainty $\|u_i\|_1\le\rho$, the inner max $\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x$ equals:
quiz.e: A linear function over the $\ell_1$ ball peaks at a vertex $\pm\rho e_j$, picking the largest $|(\Delta_ix)_j|$. The $\ell_1$ penalty belongs to box uncertainty: the norms swap.

quiz.q: Box uncertainty with $\bar a=(2,1)$, $\Delta=I$, $\rho=0.5$, and $x=(1,3)$. What is the worst-case value of $a^\top x$?
With $\Delta=I$ and the same $\rho$, how do the worst-case values $\max_{a\in U}a^\top x$ compare across budget, ellipsoidal and box sets, for any $x$?
o: It depends on the signs of $x$
quiz.e: The penalties are $\rho\|x\|_\infty\le\rho\|x\|_2\le\rho\|x\|_1$, matching the nesting $\ell_1$ ball $\subseteq\ell_2$ ball $\subseteq\ell_\infty$ ball. Box is the most conservative, not the least.

quiz.q: Without adding variables, how many linear constraints replace one budget-robust constraint $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_\infty\le b_i$ with $\Delta_i\in\mathbb R^{k_i\times n}$?
quiz.e: One constraint for each sign and each component: $\bar a_i^\top x\pm\rho(\Delta_ix)_j\le b_i$, $j=1,\dots,k_i$. $k_i$ misses the negative side of the absolute value.

quiz.q: Which robust counterpart is NOT a linear program?
quiz.e: The $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_2$ term makes it a conic program. Box and budget linearize, and polyhedral dualizes into an LP.

quiz.q: In the box LP, $t_{ij}$ satisfy $-t_{ij}\le(\Delta_ix)_j\le t_{ij}$ and $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\sum_jt_{ij}\le b_i$. Why is this equivalent to $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_1\le b_i$?
o: Feasible $t$ have $t_{ij}\ge|(\Delta_ix)_j|$, and $t_{ij}=|(\Delta_ix)_j|$ is always allowed, so $x$ is feasible in one iff in the other
At the optimum the solver sets every $t_{ij}=0$
$t_{ij}$ equals the dual variable of row $i$
quiz.e: The two bounds give $t_{ij}\ge|(\Delta_ix)_j|$, so $\sum_jt_{ij}\ge\|\Delta_ix\|_1$ with equality achievable; hence the same $x$ are feasible. Setting $t_{ij}=0$ would force $\Delta_ix=0$.

quiz.q: A polyhedral uncertainty set $\{\bar a_i+u_i: D_iu_i\le d_i\}$:
o: need not be a norm uncertainty set
quiz.e: The recitation's triangle around $\bar a=(2,2)$ is polyhedral but not a norm ball. Its counterpart is an LP, not conic.

quiz.q: What is the LP dual of the inner problem $\max_u u^\top x$ s.t. $Du\le d$, with $u$ free?
quiz.e: $\le$ constraints in a max give $p\ge0$; free primal variables give dual equalities. $p^\top D\ge x^\top$ would correspond to $u\ge0$.

quiz.q: Why can the robust constraint $\bar a^\top x+\max\{u^\top x: Du\le d\}\le b$ be replaced by '$\exists p\ge0$ with $p^\top D=x^\top$ and $\bar a^\top x+p^\top d\le b$'?
o: Strong duality makes the inner max equal the dual min, and a min is $\le c$ iff some dual-feasible $p$ achieves $\le c$
Weak duality alone makes the max equal every feasible dual objective
quiz.e: Weak duality shows any feasible $p$ certifies the bound (sufficiency); strong duality, assuming the inner problem is feasible with a finite optimum, gives necessity. Weak duality alone only gives an upper bound, not equality.

quiz.q: A direct polyhedral LP has $m=50$ rows, $n=20$ variables and $\ell_i=30$ for every $i$. How many variables and scalar constraints (excluding nonnegativity)?
quiz.e: Variables $n+\sum_i\ell_i=20+50\cdot30=1520$. Constraints $m(n+1)=50\cdot21=1050$: $n$ equalities from $p_i^\top D_i=x^\top$ plus one robust inequality per row. 1,000 forgets the robust inequalities.

quiz.q: How is the cutting-plane master problem initialized?
o: As the nominal problem, $\hat U_i=\{\bar a_i\}$
With every extreme point of each $U_i$
As the dual of the robust LP
quiz.e: Step 1 uses the nominal rows; cuts are added only when violated. Listing all extreme points is what the method avoids.

quiz.q: Cutting planes, row 1 with $U_1=\{a\in\mathbb R^2_+: a_1+a_2\le3\}$, $b_1=6$, $\varepsilon=0$. The master returns $x^*=(4,1)$. What happens next?
o: Add the cut $3x_1\le6$ (worst case $\hat a=(3,0)$ gives 12 > 6)
quiz.e: $\hat a=\arg\max_{a\in U}(4a_1+a_2)=(3,0)$ with value $12>6$, so add $3x_1\le6$, i.e. $x_1\le2$. The vertex $(0,3)$ gives only 3 and is not the worst case.

quiz.q: Why can't the cutting-plane method stop when the master is unbounded?
o: The master holds only some robust constraints, so it can be unbounded while the robust problem is finite
An unbounded master proves the robust problem is unbounded
It means the uncertainty set is empty
The method needs an infeasible master first
quiz.e: The master is a relaxation; missing cuts can leave a direction open. In the recitation example the nominal $a_1=0$ master is unbounded, yet the robust optimum is $x^*=1$.

written.q: Consider $\max c^\top x$ s.t. $\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x\le b_i$ ($i=1,\dots,m$), $x\ge0$, with box uncertainty $U_i=\{\bar a_i+\Delta_i^\top u_i: \|u_i\|_\infty\le\rho\}$. (a) Derive the robust counterpart of row $i$. (b) Rewrite the whole problem as an LP. (c) How do (a)-(b) change for budget ($\ell_1$) and ellipsoidal ($\ell_2$) sets, and which remain LPs?
written.m: (a) $\max_{a_i\in U_i}a_i^\top x=\bar a_i^\top x+\max_{\|u_i\|_\infty\le\rho}u_i^\top(\Delta_ix)$. Each $u_{ij}\in[-\rho,\rho]$ independently, so choose $u_{ij}=\rho\,\mathrm{sign}((\Delta_ix)_j)$, giving $\rho\sum_j|(\Delta_ix)_j|=\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_1$. Row $i$: $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_1\le b_i$. (b) $\max_{x,t}c^\top x$ s.t. $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}t_{ij}\le b_i$, $-t_{ij}\le(\Delta_ix)_j\le t_{ij}$ for all $i,j$, $x\ge0$, $t\ge0$ — an LP, equivalent because feasible $t_{ij}\ge|(\Delta_ix)_j|$ and equality is attainable. (c) Budget: penalty $\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_\infty$, linearized as $\bar a_i^\top x\pm\rho(\Delta_ix)_j\le b_i$ for all $j$ ($2k_i$ constraints, no new variables) — LP. Ellipsoidal: $\bar a_i^\top x+\rho\|\Delta_ix\|_2\le b_i$ — a conic program, not an LP.
k: Splits inner max into $\bar a_i^\top x+\max u_i^\top(\Delta_ix)$
Correct LP with auxiliary $t_{ij}$ and both-sided bounds

written.q: A robust LP has $m$ rows with polyhedral uncertainty $U_i=\{\bar a_i+u_i: D_iu_i\le d_i\}$, $D_i\in\mathbb R^{\ell_i\times n}$. (a) Use LP duality to give a finite reformulation of row $i$, and state the assumption you need. (b) Count variables and scalar constraints of the resulting LP and evaluate for $m=1000$, $n=100$, $\ell_i=200$. (c) Describe the cutting-plane alternative: master, separation subproblem for this set, stopping rule, and the unbounded-master case.
written.m: (a) Inner primal: $\max_{u_i}u_i^\top x$ s.t. $D_iu_i\le d_i$; dual: $\min_{p_i\ge0}p_i^\top d_i$ s.t. $p_i^\top D_i=x^\top$. Assuming the inner problem is feasible with a finite optimum, strong duality equates them, so row $i$ holds iff $\exists p_i\ge0$ with $p_i^\top D_i=x^\top$ and $\bar a_i^\top x+p_i^\top d_i\le b_i$. The robust problem becomes $\max_{x,\{p_i\}}c^\top x$ s.t. those constraints for all $i$, $x\ge0$. (b) Variables $n+\sum_i\ell_i$; constraints $m(n+1)$ ($n$ equalities plus one inequality per row). For the data: $100+1000\cdot200=200{,}100$ variables and $1000\cdot101=101{,}000$ constraints. (c) Master starts as the nominal LP in the $n$ original variables. Given $x^*$, for each row solve the LP $\max_{u_i}(\bar a_i+u_i)^\top x^*$ s.t. $D_iu_i\le d_i$ to get $\hat a_i$; if $\hat a_i^\top x^*>b_i+\varepsilon$, add $\hat a_i^\top x\le b_i$. Stop when no cut is added; $x^*$ is then robust optimal. If the master is infeasible, the robust problem is infeasible. If it is unbounded, do not stop: choose $x^*$ with $c^\top x^*>M$, separate as above and add violated cuts to block the direction.
k: Correct primal and dual inner problems
Existence of $p_i\ge0$ reformulation with feasibility/finite-optimum assumption
Separation is an LP over $U_i$; add violated cuts with tolerance
Correct handling of infeasible and unbounded master
